paragraph: Park Ridge single-family is a real seller's market right now. Twenty-nine homes sold at a median of $999,750 against a median list of $899,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.10, and 93 percent of those sales closed above asking with a median of 13 days on market. That combination means multiple offer situations on most of the good ones, and you should plan your numbers accordingly. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with two full baths, with ranches and split-levels making up much of the rest. Condos and townhouses are a much smaller slice at 10 sales, and the range runs from $390,000 to $1,820,000, so the $552,500 median is the number to anchor on. That tier is competitive without the same frenzy, a 1.02 ratio and 23 days on market, and it skews to two-bedroom, two-bath units. On the seasonal read, single-family volume built steadily into June, which is exactly the usual Bergen arc, but the individual months are too thin to call a price trend from. Treat the six-month numbers as the picture. If you're weighing the two tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a condo or townhouse.
